messages:
Ashley: Heads up — terraform applies from infra/terraform keep failing on gha for the last hour. Lots of 'Error: Another process is modifying the state' and some provider install/symlink errors. :grimacing:
Jordan: saw ~10 failures in the PR queue. These are on self-hosted runners, right?
Ashley: yes, self-hosted runners in us-west-2. It looks like actions/cache restore of .terraform is restoring a stale provider binary symlink which then breaks init. Also see state lock contention.
Morgan: can you paste the concrete error you see?
Ashley: sure — copied from runner log:
```
Error: Failed to install provider
  on registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws v3.12.0:
  failed to symlink plugin: lstat /home/runner/work/_temp/.terraform/providers/registry.terraform.io/hashicorp/aws/3.12.0/linux_amd64/terraform-provider-aws_v3.12.0: no such file or directory
Error: Another process is modifying the state (ID: 9b3f...ebc)
```
Jordan: ugh. I think there are two separate issues: cache restore corrupting the .terraform/plugins layout, and multiple apply jobs actually running in parallel against the same state/workspace.
Sam: quick note — our actions/cache key for .terraform is currently `key: ${{ hashFiles('**/*.tf') }}` which doesn't include branch or runner id. That can cause different PRs to restore the same cache.
Morgan: suggested fixes: include github.ref and runner.os in the cache key, or stop caching the whole .terraform directory and only cache the plugin download dir (if any). Also avoid caching symlinked binaries.
Jordan: also add concurrency control to the apply job. Something like:
```yaml
concurrency:
  group: infra-apply-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```
so only one apply per ref/env runs at a time.
Ashley: immediate mitigation: disabled the cache-restore step on infra/terraform workflows and requeued failing applies. Added a tiny retry wrapper around `terraform apply` with exponential backoff for transient lock errors.
ci-bot: Deploy bot: Notified. If failure rate > 50% across the infra repo, creating incident.
Sam: can we also double-check remote state locking? We use S3 + DynamoDB locks, but if runners hammer the lock table there can be latency. Might be worth adding retries around lock acquisition.
Morgan: we're using DynamoDB locks already. The 'Another process' ID was from an earlier failed run that didn't release because the runner crashed while holding the lock. Concurrency + better retries should prevent most of this.
Ashley: opening a small PR now to: 1) remove .terraform full restore, 2) use a branch-specific cache key if we still need it, 3) add concurrency group to apply, 4) add retry/backoff for terraform apply. I'll watch the queue for the next hour. :eyes:
Jordan: thanks. If this persists after the PR, we'll consider a short window where we force-serialise applies via a lightweight semaphore in S3 or switch the apply job to a dedicated runner pool.
Sam: FYI I added a runner-metrics alert for >20% job failures in us-west-2 so we get paged earlier.
Morgan: also check actions/cache version — older versions had a bug that could corrupt extracted archives when parallel restores happen on the same runner host.
Ashley: noted. I'll include a comment in the PR linking to this thread and the logs. Thanks everyone.
